messages:
alex: Heads up: hitting a weird retry queue stall on Android SDK. After a 401 from auth endpoint, subsequent requests from same client get queued for ~30s then all fail. Repro on Pixel 6 emulator.

maya: oh no. can you paste logs? sounds like authenticator sequencer or dispatcher starvation.

alex: logs: ```
okhttp.Authenticator - refreshing token
retrofit2.Call - retry enqueued
java.util.concurrent.TimeoutException: Timeout waiting for token
```
Also using coroutine dispatcher IO + OkHttpDispatcher default.

leo: Are you using synchronous Authenticator that blocks the network thread? Authenticator should return a Request quickly; do token refresh async and cancel others.

alex: We call suspend fun refreshToken() inside OkHttp Authenticator with runBlocking. Probably the cause.

jen: @alex runBlocking in Authenticator is a huge antipattern. It will block OkHttp's internal executor. Use a non-blocking token refresh or external memoized cache with single-flight.

alex: Switching to background single-flight with CompletableDeferred fixed it locally. Curious about SDK parity: Android sample app still uses blocking refresh in examples.

maya: We should update sampleapp and docs. Filing quick PR to devex samples. Also add test to emulator CI to catch runBlocking in Authenticator.

ci-bot: CI: test-emulator-auth -> failed on flaky network test (detected blocking behavior). See job 9761.

leo: :thumbsup: I'll open issue and add lint check to detect runBlocking usage inside okhttp.Authenticator class.

alex: thanks all. I'll send repro and minimal fix PR.
